newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed on Wednesday due to an uncertain short-term market trend with many investors staying on the sidelines, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 19,450 yuan ($2,344) per tonne, rising 40 yuan. It opened at 19,380 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 19,350 and a high of 19,460.
November fell 40 to 19,250 yuan, December unchanged at 19,350, February rose 50 to 19,500, March fell 10 to 19,590, April increased 30 to 19,630 and May decreased 50 to 19,600.
Combined volume fell to 31,240 tonnes from 55,400.
Copper opened mostly lower and some short-covering and fresh buying pushed prices off lows for most of the session.
Traders said most investors saw the short-term market trend as unclear and were willing to take a wait-and-see attitude.
"Despite overnight LME gains, Shanghai investors were not willing to build large amounts of fresh positions today," one trader said.
"Many investors became nervous as a result of falls in domestic A share prices and the fact that copper failed to breach the $1,900-$1,970 range on the LME," he added.

Traders said sharp falls in the short term seem impossible without parallel movement on the LME despite an over-surplus of domestic spot copper. Upward potential was also limited due to poor technical and fundamental factors.
Analysts expect copper to move around the 19,500 yuan level in the next few days.
Only 70 tonnes of aluminium's January 1997 contract traded, ending at 13,420 yuan, up 420 yuan.
